title: Fathom Analytics: Privacy-First Google Analytics Alternative
content:
[New**Meet Luna, Our AI Assistant**](/changelog/oct2026-luna)

# Analytics without the cookies
See where visitors come from, which pages they read, and what converts. **Fathom is a Google Analytics alternative that makes your analytics easy to understand and respects visitor privacy.**

[Start free trial](https://app.usefathom.com/register) [View a live demo](https://app.usefathom.com/demo)

7-day free trial · [From $15/month](/pricing) · Cancel anytime

Trusted by Microsoft, Tailwind & over a million websites

![Huberman Lab](/assets/src/customers/logo-huberman.svg)![Microsoft](/assets/src/customers/logo-microsoft.svg)![Tailwind](/assets/src/customers/logo-tailwind.svg)![Laravel](/assets/src/customers/logo-laravel.svg)

[![Fathom analytics dashboard](/_astro/dash-full-light.tnUwaPOq_1Ibj82.webp)](https://app.usefathom.com/demo)

[Learn how our dashboard works](/docs/start/dashboard)

  ![Ian Mackey](/assets/responsive/3d64b680185e98a1-80.webp)

Analytics for Huberman Lab are solely powered by Fathom. It's such a pleasure to use compared to Google Analytics. There's just the right number of features, and their platform is incredibly intuitive.

Ian Mackey, Huberman Lab   ![Ruben Gamez](/assets/responsive/458f790931a6e337-80.webp)

I consider Fathom a must have tool if you want to understand what's happening with your website traffic. It's simple, speedy, and accurate.

Ruben Gamez, founder SignWell and Bidsketch

For the longest time, website analytics software was seriously bad. It was hard to understand, time-consuming to use, and worse, it exploited visitor data for big tech to profit. We built Fathom to make analytics easy to use and respectful of privacy.

## European analytics
Our entire company is built on putting digital privacy first. Your EU traffic is automatically routed [through European-owned infrastructure](/features/data-isolation), and as a Canadian company, we're covered by Canada's EU adequacy decision. Plus, we're GDPR, CCPA, ePrivacy, PECR (and more) compliant.

## See more of your visitors
Plenty of analytics tools miss real people because of blockers, cookies and sampling. Fathom is built to show you [human visits](/features), so you get a clearer picture of who's on your site without invading anyone's privacy.

## Our script is fast
Our lightweight script loads without holding up your page. It loads from all over the world, from the place closest to the person visiting your site. Learn [how analytics affects page speed](/blog/google-analytics-seo).

## We sell software, not data
This is why we created [anonymous pageview tracking](/data) that doesn't collect or store personal data (we have no use for it). Because of this, Fathom doesn't require annoying cookie notices.

  [See all our features](/features) [Why choose Fathom?](/why-fathom-analytics/web-analytics-software) The best [Google Analytics alternative](/features/vs-google-analytics) with a focus on privacy.

## See all of your sites at a glance
See every site on your account on a single screen with our [all-sites view](/docs/features/all-sites), including totals for things like current visitors and bounce rate.

![The Fathom all-sites view with six sites, combined totals across the top and a card for each site with its own chart, visitors, pageviews, time on site, bounce rate and event completions.](/assets/responsive/eb51641465becf97-640.webp)

## Ads and newsletter campaigns
Use [UTMs](/docs/features/campaigns) to see how your ad campaigns are doing and which links in your newsletter get clicked.

![The Campaign box on a Fathom dashboard, listing UTM campaigns such as TwitterAd01, DuckBillCampaign and Newsletter-Oct30 with their visitors and views.](/assets/responsive/dcd73c367a98c274-640.webp)

## Measure your conversions
Measure the actions that matter to your business, from signups and downloads to purchases. Add [custom events](/docs/events/overview) and attach a monetary value to see more than pageviews.

![The Events box on a Fathom dashboard: PDF downloads, mailing list signups and merch purchases, with uniques, completions, conversion rate and value.](/assets/responsive/1ce69622ffdd6d19-640.webp)

## No cookie banners
Cookie banners are ugly and annoying. Fathom doesn’t use cookies, so no consent banner is required for your analytics. Learn [how we protect visitor privacy](/data).

*yoursite.com*

**We value your privacy**

We use cookies to improve your experience, personalise content and analyse our traffic.

CustomiseReject allAccept all

Fathom doesn’t use cookies.

## Send email reports
Send yourself, your customers, or your coworkers [email reports](/docs/features/email-reports) for one site or several, so anyone can keep track of your analytics without logging in.

![A monthly Fathom email report with visitors, views, time on site, bounce rate, top pages and top referrers.](/assets/responsive/91f6eea9bf6fcdf8-640.webp)

## Unlimited data retention
We keep your analytics history for as long as you’re a customer. View or [export your data](/docs/features/exporting) from the day you started using Fathom until right now, even if that’s 30 years of data.

## A lightweight script for a fast website
Your analytics shouldn’t weigh down your website. Fathom’s lightweight script helps keep pages fast while you learn what’s working. [Compare Fathom with Google Analytics](/features/vs-google-analytics).

Add it to your site’s  and you’re done

```
<script
  src="https://cdn.usefathom.com/script.js"
  data-site="ABCDEFG"
  defer></script>
```

## Trusted by 1,000,000+ websites and counting
What kind of companies use Fathom? Fortune 100s, pioneers of the Open Web, Premier League football clubs, banks, and governments around the world all use our software to provide them with a privacy-focused and easy-to-use alternative to Google Analytics. Not to mention loads of small and mighty companies are Fathom customers as well.

![GitHub](/assets/src/customers/logo-github.svg)![IBM](/assets/src/customers/logo-ibm.svg)![New York Times](/assets/src/customers/logo-nytimes.svg)![Vue.js](/assets/src/customers/logo-vue.svg)![Bosch](/assets/src/customers/logo-bosch.svg)![HashiCorp](/assets/src/customers/logo-hashicorp.svg)![Aston Villa](/assets/src/customers/logo-avfc.svg)![Transistor](/assets/src/customers/logo-transistor.svg)![Bootstrap](/assets/src/customers/logo-bootstrap.svg)![SavvyCal](/assets/src/customers/logo-savvycal.svg)![SignWell](/assets/src/customers/logo-signwell.svg)![Whitney Museum](/assets/src/customers/logo-whitney.svg)

  ![Charli Marie](/assets/responsive/1e3dbad7aef99566-80.webp)

I switched to Fathom because it's an ethical analytics tool that I trust. It gives me everything I want to know about my site's performance.

Charli Marie, Creative director of ConvertKit   ![Evan You](/assets/responsive/306aba0f000516ac-80.webp)

Our new Vue.js website has been using Fathom because I like how it's lightweight and respects user privacy.

Evan You, creator of Vue.js   ![James Brooks](/assets/responsive/2975929804b9e18a-80.webp)

Fathom is a beautiful, fast piece of software built on Laravel and it lets us see what we need right away.

James Brooks, Head of Enterprise Enablement at Laravel   ![Marshall Shorts](/assets/responsive/29009c2de8392e9e-80.webp)

I value my time and my website visitors right to privacy. That's why I've switched to Fathom Analytics.

Marshall Shorts, founder of Artfluential   ![Jon Henshaw](/assets/responsive/6ad109d79e514e98-80.webp)

Fathom simplifies the task of analyzing site performance while simultaneously respecting my visitors' privacy. Also, it's a joy to use.

Jon Henshaw, founder of Coywolf   ![Justin Jackson](/assets/responsive/4c0c15733bb0032d-80.webp)

Today, so many big tech corps are abusing our privacy. This is why I use Fathom. They're an analytics company I can trust.

Justin Jackson, Cofounder of Transistor   ![Derrick Reimer](/assets/responsive/d4d109a6d475b450-80.webp)

Privacy-protections aside, I love the beautifully simple interface. Fathom is now part of my default stack.

Derrick Reimer, founder of SavvyCal   ![Jessica Joyce](/assets/responsive/97877bf4cdf23894-80.webp)

They are the best Google Analytics alternative who really care about privacy and simplicity. Fathom's simple dashboard with clear metrics makes it easy to understand what's happening across all web properties.

Jessica Joyce, SEO expert   ![Nathalie Lussier](/assets/responsive/4f5e8cc50f111f4c-80.webp)

Fathom Analytics is a great Google Analytics alternative because it is focused on protecting visitors' privacy and does not bog down loading times, leading to faster websites.

Nathalie Lussier, founder of AccessAlly.com   ![Caleb Porzio](/assets/responsive/65f0317e23cf661a-80.webp)

After switching to Fathom for my web properties, I find I'm more attentive to my sites because I'm always aware of how many people are on them and which pages are most popular.

Caleb Porzio, creator of Alpine.js

## Getting started with Fathom is easy
You'll be looking at real numbers in a few minutes, without spying on anyone. And if you get stuck, our support team is always on hand to help you get up and running.

  Step 1

### Sign up for an account
Start with a 7-day free trial, then [pricing](/pricing) starts at $15/month.

  Step 2

### Add our script
It's [a single line of code](/docs/script/embed) that works with every site, web app and CMS. You can run it alongside your current analytics while you try Fathom.

  Step 3

### See your stats
Your [Fathom dashboard](/docs/start/dashboard) will start showing you real-time data. Moving from Google Analytics? You can [bring your GA4 history with you](/features/ga-importer).

## Fathom [integrates](/docs/integrations) easily with all content management systems and developer frameworks
[![Carrd](/assets/src/integrations/logo-carrd.svg)](/docs/integrations/carrd) [![Kit](/assets/src/integrations/logo-convertkit.svg)](/docs/integrations/kit) [![Ember](/assets/src/integrations/logo-ember.svg)](/docs/integrations/ember) [![Gatsby](/assets/src/integrations/logo-gatsby.svg)](/docs/integrations/gatsby) [![Inertia](/assets/src/integrations/logo-inertia.svg)](/docs/integrations/inertiajs) [![Next](/assets/src/integrations/logo-next.svg)](/docs/integrations/next) [![Nuxt](/assets/src/integrations/logo-nuxt.svg)](/docs/integrations/nuxt) [![SavvyCal](/assets/src/integrations/logo-savvycal.svg)](/docs/integrations/savvycal) [![Transistor](/assets/src/integrations/logo-transistor.svg)](/docs/integrations/transistor) [![Webflow](/assets/src/integrations/logo-webflow.svg)](/docs/integrations/webflow) [![Vue](/assets/src/integrations/logo-vue.svg)](/docs/integrations/vue) [![WordPress](/assets/src/integrations/logo-wp.svg)](/docs/integrations/wordpress) [![Drupal](/assets/src/integrations/logo-drupal.svg)](/docs/integrations/drupal) [![Discourse](/assets/src/integrations/logo-discourse.svg)](/docs/integrations/discourse)

We built Fathom from the very start to be privacy-focused and easy to use. Our business model is honest yet unusual for the startup scene: we charge a fair price for our software (instead of giving it away for free, then selling your data to generate revenue).

Our customers come first because they're our only investors. We don't have venture capital funding, bank loans, or other shareholders we answer to. Instead, we're happily independent and bootstrapped.

We grow sustainably when our customers tell their friends about Fathom, agencies start using us for all their client websites, or when reviewers try several analytics products and end up choosing us. This is the way we like it.

By supporting a company like ours, you are taking a step towards a shared vision of the internet that aligns with ours: away from the watchful eyes of big tech, based on trust and privacy, and all without compromising reliability, speed or quality of support.

Fathom began as an idea that a tech company could be run and grow while staying true to its values. It started as an analytics product that could be privacy-focused and simple without losing the value of its data.

We're proud of how we run our business, sell our product and serve our customers. And of course, we hope you'll join us.

[Jack Ellis](/author/jack-ellis),
founder of Fathom

## Frequently asked questions
Can I use the same plan for multiple websites?

Yes. Sites on a plan share your monthly pageviews. The larger pageview plans include more sites, and you can add extra site packs from billing if you need them.

 How long do you store my analytics data?

Forever, as long as you are a customer. You can access your data all the way back to when you signed up. 7 days, or even 30 days, doesn't show you if your site is trending up or down, which is why we keep your analytics history. Export it before you cancel if you leave.

 Why is Fathom better than European-only providers?

Our [data isolation](/features/data-isolation) routes EU visitor traffic through EU infrastructure. Visitors elsewhere are routed through our global infrastructure, so they can connect closer to home. This helps keep analytics fast for visitors around the world.

 What happens if I go over my pageview limit?

We never charge for occasional traffic spikes, and we don't shut your account off if you hit your plan limit early. If you stay well over your limit, we'll email you about a larger plan, and you choose whether to upgrade. We send a few friendly reminders and extra time before we pause dashboard and API access, and we keep collecting your data throughout. See our [plan-limits guide](/docs/account/limits) for the details.

 Why isn't Fathom free like Google Analytics?

If you aren't paying for a product, you are the product. That's why Google Analytics is free, because they make enough money off the personal data their customers give them by using their analytics service. We charge a small and sustainable fee for Fathom because our business model is selling software, not data. Our customers gladly pay for our service because they know their data is safe with us and their visitors' privacy is protected.

 Why does digital privacy even matter?

You may think that digital privacy doesn't matter because you have nothing to hide. And that may be true (to some extent), but your data shouldn't be monetised and sold by giant tech companies who are taking your tastes and preferences and selling them to advertisers. By using Fathom, you are making your website [a black hole to big tech](/blog/blackhole), meaning they cannot track any data about individuals who visit your website.

 Want to learn more about Fathom?

Need more information? We've got you covered:

- Here's why Fathom is [a great Google Analytics alternative](/features/vs-google-analytics).
- Wait, what are [simple website analytics](/why-fathom-analytics/simple-web-analytics)?
- How is Fathom [GDPR, CCPA and PECR compliant website analytics](/legal/compliance)?
- Why is Fathom a [privacy-focused web analytics tool](/why-fathom-analytics/privacy-focused-web-analytics)?
- How do [cookieless analytics](/why-fathom-analytics/cookieless-analytics) actually work?

## Website analytics deserved better, so we built something better
Fathom shows you what's working on your website without tracking the people who visit it. It's trusted by Fortune 100s, banks, governments and companies of every size. Start with a 7-day free trial, then plans start at $15/month.

[Start free trial](https://app.usefathom.com/register) [View a live demo](https://app.usefathom.com/demo)

## Frequently asked questions
How does the 7-day trial work?

Choose a plan and add your card to start a 7-day free trial. Your card is not charged until the trial ends, and we’ll email you before your plan starts billing. Your subscription then renews automatically unless you cancel in your account settings. You can run Fathom alongside your existing analytics while you try it.

 How do I cancel my account or trial?

We’re not interested in having someone’s money if they aren’t happy. You can cancel anytime, right from your account settings. You don’t have to call or email us (unless you have a question). There are no contracts, and you can export your data before cancelling.

 What happens if I hit my pageview limit?

We’ll never turn your analytics off for occasional traffic spikes. If you stay well over your limit, we’ll email you about a larger plan, and you decide whether to upgrade or cancel (no hard feelings either way). We send a few friendly reminders and extra time before we pause dashboard and API access, and we keep collecting your data throughout. See our [plan-limits guide](/docs/account/limits) for the details.

 Do custom events count towards my pageview limit?

Yes. If you use custom events on your website or send them through our API, each one counts towards your monthly pageview allowance.

 How many sites does my plan include?

Every plan includes at least 50 sites, and bigger plans include more. Select a plan above to see exactly how many. If you need more, you can add up to 15 packs of 50 extra sites yourself from your billing settings, at $10/month or $100/year per pack. Need to go really big? [Get in touch](/about/contact) and we’ll sort you out.

 Can I change my pageview limit?

Of course! If you exceed your limit for two months in a row, we’ll get in touch about a larger plan. Or, if you’re under your current tier for two months in a row (and it’s not our lowest tier already), you can move to a smaller plan from your billing settings.

 Can I explore Fathom before signing up?

We don’t do sales calls or live demos, but our software is ridiculously easy to use. You can watch our [10-minute walkthrough](/video/dashboard-walkthrough), click around the [live dashboard](https://app.usefathom.com/demo) or give Fathom a 7-day free trial alongside your existing analytics. Every feature is [documented](/docs), and if you have specific questions, we’re here by [email](/about/contact).

 Do you offer a free plan?

Nope, and here’s why: we’ve invested heavily in fast, reliable infrastructure (we don’t host Fathom on cheap servers that go offline). Our business model is selling software, not your data, so we’ve priced Fathom to be sustainable for a very long time.

 Have another question?

[Reach out](/about/contact)! We’re happy to help with any pre-sales questions.

Today, so many big tech corps are abusing our privacy. This is why I use Fathom. They're an analytics company I can trust.

Justin Jackson, Cofounder of Transistor  ![Nathalie Lussier](/assets/responsive/4f5e8cc50f111f4c-80.webp)

title: Website Analytics Features - Fathom Analytics
content:
# A Google Analytics alternative that’s privacy-focused and cookie-free
Fathom helps you understand your website visitors without spying on them. That’s why thousands of companies, from bootstrapped software companies to Fortune 100s, trust Fathom for their website analytics.

![Microsoft](/assets/src/customers/logo-microsoft.svg)![GitHub](/assets/src/customers/logo-github.svg)![IBM](/assets/src/customers/logo-ibm.svg)![Laravel](/assets/src/customers/logo-laravel.svg)![Tailwind](/assets/src/customers/logo-tailwind.svg)![HashiCorp](/assets/src/customers/logo-hashicorp.svg)![New York Times](/assets/src/customers/logo-nytimes.svg)![Bootstrap](/assets/src/customers/logo-bootstrap.svg)

### Don’t clutter your website with cookie banners
You don’t need a consent banner that annoys visitors, clutters your layout and slows the page down. Fathom [doesn’t use cookies](/why-fathom-analytics/cookieless-analytics), so you can keep analytics on your site without the pop-up.

### Protect the privacy of your website visitors
We’re GDPR, ePrivacy, PECR and CCPA compliant because digital privacy sits at the core of the product. We’ve had privacy lawyers vet how we collect and store data, and EU visitor data is processed in the EU automatically.

[Read about data isolation](/features/data-isolation)

### See humans, not bots
We filter out bots, crawlers, DDoS junk and other non-human traffic, so your dashboard is a picture of people who actually visited. Data shows up in real time, not 24 to 48 hours later.

### Get the information you need to make decisions
See which pages are popular, who’s sending traffic, which campaigns are converting and which events are paying off, all from one dashboard. Add a filter and you can drill into a campaign, a country or a single page in a click.

[Learn how our dashboard works](/docs/start/dashboard)

   [![Fathom analytics dashboard](/assets/responsive/1c538bf0909168e6-480.webp)](https://app.usefathom.com/demo)      [Start free trial](https://app.usefathom.com/register) [View a live demo](https://app.usefathom.com/demo)  7-day free trial    No cookie notices required    GDPR compliant

### Save the filters you use every week
Want to check your blog traffic, a campaign or visitors from a particular country? Combine filters, give the view a name and open it again in one click. Everyone with access to that site can use the same saved views.

[Saved views](/docs/features/saved-views)

### Put your traffic changes in context
Mark a launch, a redesign or a press mention on your chart with a milestone. Compare dates to see how traffic changed from the previous week, month or year, or choose your own periods.

[Milestones](/docs/features/milestones)   [Date comparisons](/docs/how-tos/compare-dates)

### Track signups, sales and their value
Record newsletter signups, form submissions and purchases as events. Send a value with a purchase and choose the currency for your events, so you can see sales totals alongside completion counts.

[Event tracking](/features/event-tracking)

### See which campaigns bring people to your site
Use UTM tags to tell your newsletters, ads and social campaigns apart. Filter the dashboard by a campaign to see its traffic, the pages people visited and the events they completed.

[UTM tracking](/features/utm-tracking)

### Send reports to your clients automatically
Schedule weekly or monthly emails for yourself, colleagues or clients. Send a report for one website, or bring several sites together in the same email. Each recipient gets the sites you select.

[Email reports](/docs/features/email-reports)

### Look after all your websites in one place
Every plan includes at least 50 sites, with extra packs available. Check them together in the all-sites view, then open a site for the details. Share individual dashboards publicly or protect them with a password.

[All-sites view](/docs/features/all-sites)   [Dashboard sharing](/docs/features/shared-dashboards)

### Use your data outside the dashboard
Download CSV files for a spreadsheet or report, or use our API to bring Fathom data into your own tools. Your analytics should be useful wherever you work.

[CSV exports](/docs/features/exporting)   [API documentation](/api)

### Bring Google Analytics and Search Console with you
Import historical GA4 data, and connect Google Search Console to see search terms, clicks, impressions and search positions alongside your website analytics.

[GA importer](/features/ga-importer)   [Search Console](/docs/features/google-search-console)

### Add Fathom to the tools you already use
Use Fathom with WordPress, Ghost, Webflow, Next.js, Nuxt and plenty more. Add one line of JavaScript, or use one of our integrations if you’d rather not touch templates.

[Browse integrations](/docs/integrations)

### Keep your pages light
Our small script loads asynchronously, so it doesn’t hold up the rest of your page. You can measure your traffic without adding a bulky analytics script.

[Install the script](/docs/script/embed)

### Keep your history
Every plan includes ongoing data retention. Come back to an old campaign, compare this year with last year, or see how far your site has come since you first installed Fathom.

[Account questions](/docs/account/faq)

### Infrastructure that keeps up when you go viral
A launch or a popular post can bring a lot of visitors at once. Fathom is built to handle traffic spikes and large websites, so you can keep an eye on what’s happening.

[Analytics for high-traffic sites](/high-traffic)

    [Start free trial](https://app.usefathom.com/register) [View a live demo](https://app.usefathom.com/demo)  7-day free trial    No cookie notices required    GDPR compliant

### Have something specific in mind?
Our [help centre](/docs) covers the details, including [multi-domain tracking](/docs/features/multi), [excluding your own traffic](/docs/script/firewall) and more. If you’re not sure whether Fathom fits what you need, [ask us](/contact).

## Frequently asked questions about Fathom
Does Fathom Analytics use cookies?

No. That’s why you don’t need a consent banner for analytics. You can read more about how we process data on our [data journey page](/data).

 Is Fathom Analytics GDPR compliant?

Yes. Privacy law comes before features we could otherwise build. You can read more about [our GDPR-compliant website analytics](/legal/compliance/gdpr-compliant-website-analytics).

 What is Fathom doing with my data?

We’re open about how data is processed and stored. Our anonymisation methods are documented, and EU visitor data is handled with [data isolation](/features/data-isolation).

 Can I host the data locally?

No. Fathom is a hosted product so we can process pageviews on a global CDN, keep dashboards fast, and process EU visitor data in the EU. Everyone else is routed to the closest region.

 Who owns my data?

You do. We sell software, not data. Other analytics products can afford to be “free” because they profit from what they collect about your visitors.

 How do I opt out of being counted?

Fathom doesn’t track individuals. We anonymise data with [hashes and salts](/docs/troubleshooting/hashes-salts). If you still don’t want your own visits on a dashboard, [block your IP](/docs/script/firewall#ip) or run a small script from your browser console. You can also set Fathom to [honour DNT](/docs/script/script-advanced#dnt).

 Do you support goal tracking?

Yes. They’re called [events](/docs/events/overview), and you can use them for newsletter signups, link clicks or ecommerce sales.

 Can I import Google Analytics into Fathom?

Yes. Our [GA importer](/features/ga-importer) brings GA4 data into Fathom so you can keep the history after Google deletes it. The import is done in a privacy-focused way.

 Can I connect Google Search Console?

Yes. Link your site and you’ll see search terms, countries, devices and pages alongside your analytics. [Here’s how to set it up](/docs/features/google-search-console).

title: Why Fathom Analytics is a great Matomo alternative

# Why Fathom Analytics is a great Matomo alternative
Matomo, formerly called Piwik, is an open-source alternative to Google Analytics. It gained traction early as an open-sourced website stats analysis project.

Fathom Analytics is newer and started in 2018 as another alternative to Google Analytics. So why should you consider Fathom Analytics over Matomo? And what are the differences between Fathom Analytics and Matomo (Piwik)? Well, let's [dive into those details](#similarities) so you can decide for yourself.

![Fathom Analytics dashboard](/assets/responsive/3afaf0e7a7b67877-640.webp)   On this page

## What are the similarities between Matomo and Fathom Analytics?
We know that [Fathom is an excellent alternative to Google Analytics](/features/vs-google-analytics), and we list the differences between both website analysis tools on our website.

Compared to Matomo and Fathom Analytics, these tools are more similar. After all, neither is an advertising monopolistic company like Google. Let's look at why that is before we explore the differences.

### Both are focused on digital privacy
Matomo, like Fathom Analytics, protects your data and customers' [digital privacy](/why-fathom-analytics/privacy-focused-web-analytics). Both website analytics software were built with digital privacy and [GDPR compliance](/legal/compliance/gdpr-compliant-website-analytics) in mind. These products help bring awareness to the need for more digital privacy and protection from online advertisers using our personal data against us.

And, because any website owner can be fined a percentage of their yearly revenue for data/privacy breaches, compliance with the EU's GDPR ([Article 83](https://gdpr.fan/a28)) is essential.

Matomo's software has a GDPR manager and IP anonymization; most importantly, the data is not used for other purposes (unlike Google Analytics). However, these features require setup and knowledge to be used correctly.

Fathom Analytics is also built from the ground up to comply with GDPR in that we only process personal data for our own purposes as a controller (e.g., relating to customer invoices). When we process visitor data through our website analytics (as a data processor), we anonymize and practice data minimization.

You can learn more about [the personal data we process and briefly pseudonymize](/legal/compliance/gdpr-compliant-website-analytics). With Fathom Analytics, there's no setup or knowledge required to comply with GDPR; that happens by default for every customer on every plan.

### Both allow you to own and control your own data
With Fathom Analytics and Matomo, you (the customer) are entirely in control and own your data for all website stats collected. That means you can export that data, delete/wipe it, or keep it forever (as long as you're a customer).

While Matomo on-premise has unlimited data retention, their cloud/hosted product only keeps your data for up to 24 months. That means if you're a customer for five years, they'll delete your first three years of data. With Fathom Analytics, our data retention policy is forever. This means that as long as you're a paying customer, you can view and export your data from the day you started collecting it. Export your data before cancelling; cancellation queues your data for deletion.

### Both let you import your Google Analytics data
Matomo and Fathom Analytics let you import your Google Analytics 4 data. (Google deleted Universal Analytics data in July 2024.)

Matomo's import process is quite involved and requires you to generate an API key inside Google Cloud's developer console. For non-developers, this is a relatively complex series of steps.

On the other hand, [Fathom's Google Analytics importer has a few simple steps](/docs/features/ga-importer). You simply authorize your Google Analytics account (by clicking a button), select which sites you want to import, and then run the import. That's it!

## What makes Fathom Analytics a great alternative to Matomo?
While there are similarities (as listed above) between Matomo and Fathom Analytics, let's now explore the differences and why we believe that Fathom Analytics is a great Matomo alternative.

### Matomo is like a full version of Google Analytics
One of the most fundamental differences is how Fathom Analytics and Matomo approach what data we collect and how it's displayed to customers.

If you look at Matomo's central dashboard, there are dozens of links to pages of reports. It's as complicated as Google Analytics. There are lots of charts, features, and a vast number of metrics available. With 12 main sections and over 70 individual reports, there's a lot of data to look at in Matomo's software.

This amount of data makes sense for some data analysts or full-time statisticians. For many other website owners, small business owners and entrepreneurs, that's too much information to look through daily (and most wouldn't).

### Fathom Analytics is a simple, easy-to-use website analytics tool
Beyond a focus on privacy for Fathom Analytics, our second goal is that [our software is simple](/why-fathom-analytics/simple-web-analytics). That means we've made it simple to use, easy to understand, and quick to learn.

That's why our dashboard is a single page of data. It's manageable, without metrics most website owners don't need or care about. Our website analytics software focuses on showing our customers only the information they need to make quick business decisions.

The Fathom Analytics dashboard focuses on live visitors, total visitors, pageviews, the top pages, referrers, countries, devices, browsers, events, and UTM campaigns. [You can watch a full dashboard demo](/video/dashboard-walkthrough) (about 8 minutes long).

You can also filter your data, generate email reports for it, [and so much more](/features).

## Website analytics optimized for speed and SEO
Any script, plugin, or resource you add to your website adds extra file size, page weight, and loading time. That means every KB should be essential and as minimal and fast-loading as possible to keep your site speedy.

That's why Fathom Analytics embed code is minimal (just a few KB) and loads deferred (so it doesn't hurt your PageSpeed score). We load our script via our lightning-fast CDN, so it loads quickly whether you're in Europe or anywhere else in the world. [Using Fathom Analytics doesn't hurt your SEO](/docs/troubleshooting/seo).

On the other hand, Matomo's script is over 20KB (50KB if you use more of their features). While it also loads deferred, you must set up your own CDN to host your Matomo script file to load as quickly from anywhere in the world as Fathom Analytics embed code.

## Privacy regulations and cookie notices for GDPR
Fathom Analytics collects fewer data points than Matomo and [anonymizes that personal data](/blog/anonymization), too. Our embed code doesn't use cookies and was built from the start to focus on [compliance with GDPR](/legal/compliance) and other privacy laws.

The most significant point here is that Fathom Analytics doesn't require a cookie consent notice to comply with GDPR (which also saves you page loading time because you don't have to install/use a cookie consent manager).

Matomo, being that it's a full-blown Google Analytics-like website analysis tool, uses cookies and requires GDPR consent notices unless you take several steps to avoid it:

- Anonymize visitor's IP addresses (Fathom does this by default).
- Anonymize URLs with personal identifiers in URL parameters (Fathom does this by default).
- Disable cookies (Fathom doesn't even use cookies, ever).
- Anonymize precise location data from the full IP address (Fathom does this by default).
- Anonymize keystrokes on forms on your site (Fathom never tracks keystrokes).

And so, if you don't take the above steps in Matomo, you can't be GDPR compliant without a cookie consent notice. With Fathom Analytics, you're compliant without a cookie consent notice by default because we don't do any of the above.

title: Keep EU visitors’ personal data in the EU
content:
# Keep EU visitors’ personal data in the EU
Lots of analytics software claims to comply with various privacy laws, such as GDPR, PECR or the ePrivacy Directive, but most of them are putting you and your website visitors at risk.

Data Isolation was built in collaboration with EU legal experts, and is part of our commitment to simplify your compliance.

EU visitors’ personal data stays in the EU. Anonymized analytics are stored on our US infrastructure. Privacy laws will keep changing, and we want to process data in the country it belongs. The EU and the US are the two biggest markets for that today. This feature exists for all customers on all plans and happens without any programming or setup required.

## Here’s why Fathom is your best option for GDPR compliance
No other analytics software goes to the measures we do to comply with GDPR, and do it in a way that doesn’t hurt your SEO or page speed load times.

|  | Google Analytics | Other analytics | Fathom |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Protects visitor personal data | No | Sometimes | Yes |
| Anonymises visitor logs | No | Sometimes | Yes |
| Processes EU traffic in the EU | No | Sometimes | Yes |
| Processes US traffic in the US | Yes | Yes | Yes |

[Start free trial](https://app.usefathom.com/register) [View a live demo](https://app.usefathom.com/demo)  7-day free trial    No cookie notices required    GDPR compliant

## Why data isolation matters
It doesn’t matter if an analytics company is located in the EU. What matters more is how and where they process data and whether EU visitor IP addresses reach US-servers.

**If you’re a company in the EU**, all of your EU traffic is processed on our EU servers, located within EU borders, ensuring your visitors' IP addresses never reach US infrastructure.

**If you’re a company outside the EU**, then you still will no doubt have visitors from the EU. Fathom takes care of routing all your EU visitors to EU-servers for you, automatically.

Since Fathom is a Canadian corporation (eh), we’ve implemented strict Data Isolation, allowing you to comply with GDPR while ensuring EU visitor IP addresses never reach US-servers.

![Data isolation explained: EU visitors are hashed and anonymised in the EU, then stored as anonymous data. Visitors outside the EU are anonymised on US servers.](/assets/responsive/1ce5b093f8bffeaa-640.webp)

## Data Isolation means intelligently routing your visitors
Fathom’s Data Isolation method works by intelligently routing visitors to the right place to process their data. When we say “data,” we’re talking about the user’s IP address, which, along with a User-Agent, could be used to potentially identify an individual in the EU, making it “personal data.”

1. **If a visitor is outside the EU**, our EU-owned CDN (Bunny.net) sends their pageview to our US servers directly and anonymizes their "data" (IP address).
2. **If a visitor is inside the EU**, our CDN sends their pageview to our European servers and anonymizes their data immediately. The IP address (personal data under GDPR) is stripped from the request inside of the EU and never reaches our US infrastructure. The anonymous data is then stored on our main US servers for fast and easy retrieval on our customer dashboards, but there’s zero personal data associated with any of it.

In all scenarios, Fathom fully protects the privacy of every website visitor’s personal information.

You can read more about [our data journey](/data) and [compliance practices](/legal/compliance).

![In every case, Fathom anonymises visitor data before it is stored.](/assets/responsive/807cc74c17de8037-640.webp)

Join thousands of companies already using Fathom Analytics

![Bootstrap](/assets/src/customers/logo-bootstrap.svg) ![IBM](/assets/src/customers/logo-ibm.svg) ![HashiCorp](/assets/src/customers/logo-hashicorp.svg) ![GitHub](/assets/src/customers/logo-github.svg) ![New York Times](/assets/src/customers/logo-nytimes.svg) ![Laravel](/assets/src/customers/logo-laravel.svg)

## Frequently asked questions (and answers)
How fast and reliable is your EU infrastructure?

Our EU Cloud is monitored 24/7, highly available, multi-region and has enough capacity to process Bieber-level traffic. And, as usual, this feature is available to all customers on all plans.

 How do I enable Data Isolation?

If you’re a Fathom customer, then congratulations, you’re already using Data Isolation and complying with privacy laws! We enable this by default for everyone on every plan.

 Is Data Isolation available to me on my current plan?

Yes. Every plan includes Data Isolation, including the smallest. It’s enabled by default.

 Why process and anonymize an IP address in the first place?

Whenever you visit a website, your IP address and User-Agent are sent to that website's servers (that's just how the internet works). Some websites retain raw logs of that information, keeping tabs on what you're browsing. Whilst others (i.e Fathom Analytics) guarantee that your visit is anonymized and not used against you. You can read more about this on our [data journey](/data).

# Blocking local/test environments
If you use local, staging, or test environments, you can keep those visits out of Fathom so your analytics only reflect real traffic to your live website. This also prevents non-live pageviews from counting against your plan quota.

### [Exclude non-live environments with allowed domains](#allowed)
The best option is to add your live website to [Allowed domains in your site firewall settings](/docs/script/firewall#allowed). Once allowed domains are set, Fathom filters out data from any hostname that is not on that list, including local, staging, and test domains.

Make sure you enter the exact version of your live domain that your site uses by default, including `www.` or the non-`www` version (or both). If your live site uses both a root domain and subdomains, add each version you want to allow.

### [Filter your IP address](#ip)
If you are the only person testing your staging or local environments, you can also [exclude visits from your IP address](/docs/script/firewall#ip). This works well for a single developer or a small, stable set of IP addresses, but allowed domains are more reliable for teams and changing networks.

### [Block tracking in your browser](#browser)
If you only need to block tracking in your current browser, open your browser console on a page where Fathom is installed and run:

```
fathom.blockTrackingForMe();
```

This stores the setting in your browser’s local storage, so it will keep working for future visits from that browser. You can [read the full browser console instructions](/docs/script/exclude-visits#console), including how to turn tracking back on later.

### [Test your exclusions](#test)
After setting up an exclusion, visit your non-live environment and check that the visit does not appear in your dashboard. Fathom shows analytics in real time, so if the exclusion is working, your non-live visit should not show up as a current visitor.

# Site firewall settings
Some settings, like canonicals and DNT can be adjusted in your [embed script’s advanced settings](/docs/script/script-advanced). Other settings (like the ones below) can be adjusted from within your Fathom account.

To adjust your firewall settings, go to `Settings`, then `Sites`, click on your site, then click the `Firewall` tab. Open a list tab (Pages, IPs, Referrers, Domains, Countries, or Events). Choose `Block` or `Allow` the following values, then add them. An empty list does not filter.

Note: If you've blocked pages, IPs, domains, or countries, visitors coming from those sources will still be able to access and navigate around your site, but their visits just won't be shown as data in your Fathom dashboard.

### [Pages](#pages)
To block a page, multiple pages or use wildcards to block pages, open the `Pages` tab, choose `Block` the following pages, then add the pathname. For example:

```
/about/
/contact/
```

The above would block both of those pages. If you wanted to block all the pages under the `/about` page, so pages like `/about/team` and `/about/luna` and so on, you’d add a wildcard:

```
/about/*
```

For blocked pages, you can’t add the domain (hostname) or http:// or https://, just add the path after the domain. If a visitor to your site goes to a blocked page, that pageview will not be tracked. If they’re a current visitor, it’ll show them as still on the previous page (as their view of the new page was blocked).

Visitors who visit blocked pages do not count as pageviews, so they do not count against your payment plan allotment of pageviews.

### [IPs](#ip)
To block your IP, someone else’s IP, or a group of IPs, open the `IPs` tab, choose `Block` the following IPs, then add the IP. The next visit after you save uses the new list.

For example:

```
100.100.100.100
200.200.200.200
```

The above would block both of those IP addresses. That means if one of them was yours and you visited your website, your visit would not show up on the dashboard stats. If you wanted to block a group of IP addresses, you could use a wildcard:

```
100.100.100.*
```

That means anyone with an IP address that started with `100.100.100.` would be blocked. So `100.100.100.1`, `100.100.100.123`, etc, would all be blocked.

**Note:** Currently only IPv4 addresses are supported for wildcards

### [Countries](#country)
Like IP blocking, you can block specific visits from anyone within a country. Open the `Countries` tab and choose `Block` the following countries.

Why would you do this? Say you’re getting a ton of traffic from a country that your business doesn’t serve; add that country to the list. They’ll still be able to see your website, but their page views and analytics data won’t show up in Fathom.

To keep only some countries, choose `Allow` the following countries and add the countries you serve.

### [Referrers](#referrers)
Similar to IP and country blocking, you can also block pageviews and events that come from specific referrers. This is useful if you notice you’re receiving a lot of spam traffic from a given site, and you want to ensure that traffic is not recorded in your analytics.

To block a referrer, open the `Referrers` tab, choose `Block` the following referrers, then add the domain of the referrer. For example, to prevent recording traffic originating from `example.com` and `spam-website.com`, you would add:

```
example.com
spam-website.com
```

You can also use wildcards to block a group of referrers. For example, to block all subdomains of `example.com`, you would add:

```
*.example.com
```

### [Domains](#allowed)
If you want to only allow data to be collected from specific domains, open the `Domains` tab, leave `Allow` the following domains selected, then add the hosts. Domains should be entered one per line (no commas).

**Once you add one or more allowed domains, this means data coming from any other domain will be blocked instantly**. This is useful if you do not want to collect data from your local development environment or are worried that other people may be using your script (by accident or otherwise).

We support wildcards here too, so if you want to allow all subdomains, you can use:

```
*.example.com
```

This then allows only subdomains of example.com, so: `subdomain.example.com` and `www.example.com`, etc. But note: using `*.example.com` would not allow `example.com`, so be careful.

If you want to only allow data from your site and use both the root domain and subdomains, you’d allow:

```
*.example.com
example.com
```

And that would cover all subdomains and your root domain.

### [Events](#events)
Use the `Events` tab to drop junk or unwanted event names at collect time, or to collect only the names you send on purpose.

1. Open `Settings`, then your site, then `Firewall`, then `Events`.
2. Choose `Block` or `Allow` the following events.
3. Add one event name per line. Wildcards (`*`) are supported.

**Block** drops those names and still collects every other event. **Allow** collects only the names (and wildcard patterns) on the list. An empty allow list collects every event.

This is useful when bots or scrapers fire junk names (path traversal strings, shell probes, and similar). Those names will not be stored once they match the list.

If you send dynamic names (for example Shopify product titles), use a wildcard such as `Product *` on an allow list. A tight allow list of exact names will drop those dynamic events.

Event name filters apply to both `fathom.trackEvent('Name')` and leftover `trackGoal` codes, once we know the event name. The next event after you save uses the new list.

To give an event its own currency, click the currency icon on the Events box on your dashboard (see [Setting a default event currency](/docs/events/overview#currency)). Currency settings do not collect or drop events.

### [Spam already in your reports](#removed-spam)
The firewall stops future visits. To clean up spam that’s already in your reports, use `Data removals` in your site’s `Manage` settings. See [Data removals](/docs/features/data-removals).

# EU isolation
If you want to use [EU isolation](https://usefathom.com/features/data-isolation), congratulations; as a Fathom customer, you’re already using it, and it’s enabled by default!

There’s nothing you have to set up or tweak or even change in [your embed script](/docs/script/embed) to use it. Fathom automatically and intelligently routes data from EU visitors to be processed in the EU and all other visitors to be processed in the US.

EU isolation provides compliance and speed in loading your script and processing the data.

It includes visitors from the following non-eu member nations:

- Iceland
- Liechtenstein
- Norway
- Switzerland
- United Kingdom

### [Our EU server locations](#servers)
- Falkenstein
- Helsinki
- Nuremberg

### [Extreme EU Isolation](#extreme)
If you need to use Extreme EU Isolation, where all global traffic is routed through the EU, please use `https://cdn-eu.usefathom.com/script.js` instead.
